questions.question: How deep should the fork-script review be?

options.label: Triage scan (Recommended)
options.description: Spawn an Explore agent: read-only pass over session_fork.py, session_fork_all.py, session_resume.py + their tests. Output a prioritized punch list (severity × effort). 5-10 min. Fold must-fixes into Phase B; backlog the rest.

options.label: Deep audit
options.description: Full code review of all 3 modules + the Phase B refactor targets in config.py/installer.py. Includes proposing test gaps and edge-case fixes. 20-30 min. More thorough but bigger context spend.

options.label: Skip review, fix known bugs only
options.description: Phase B as scoped, plus the 2 known session_resume bugs. Don't go looking for more. Fastest.

transcript_tail.text: 4 Terminal tabs should now have `claude -r <fork>` actually running. If those work, the `--open-terminal` bug fix is another Phase B item.

Phase B task updated to include both `session_resume` bugs (the `--open-app` silent-drop + `--open-terminal` no-op-on-Terminal.app). Ready to start the refactor when you confirm those 4 terminals are running `claude -r` now.
kinda worked, but required interaction (resume from summary)

That's the expected `claude -r` UX — Claude always shows the summary + confirm prompt before resuming a session (intentional safety, no `--auto-continue` flag exists in the CLI for `-r`). So "kinda worked, but required interaction" is the best you can get from `claude -r` today; nothing to fix on our side.

(Side note for the future: `claude --fork-session -r <uuid>` is a built-in flag that resumes + assigns a new session id, but it doesn't do the cwd-relocation our `fork-all --into-main` does — different tool.)

Ready to start Phase B (the host-derived defaults + docs revalidation in the worktree)?
should we review the fork scripts?
